power-automate-trigger.title: Introduction to triggers – Power Automate – Microsoft Learn
power-automate-trigger.notes: A trigger is the event that starts a cloud flow in Power Automate, for example the arrival of an email that then causes a notification to be posted in Microsoft Teams. Connectors such as SharePoint and Outlook usually supply ready-made triggers; the Office 365 Outlook connector, for instance, offers one that fires when a new email arrives. The documentation groups flows by how they are started. Automated flows run after an event occurs, such as a post on social media containing a chosen keyword. Instant flows are started manually by pressing a button, either in Power Automate or in the mobile app, using the manual trigger. Scheduled flows run at a set time or on a repeating basis, such as every morning or every Monday, and use the Recurrence trigger, where frequency and start date and time are chosen before the flow is created. Typical examples are a keyword alert by email, a button-press reminder for a daily team meeting and a weekly project report. After the trigger, the flow continues with actions. The page does not cover licensing, prerequisites or limits.

power-bi-org-apps.title: Org apps in Microsoft Fabric and Power BI – Microsoft Learn
power-bi-org-apps.notes: Org apps are a newer evolution of workspace apps, implemented as a Fabric item type, and they coexist with workspace apps without replacing or migrating them. Creators use them to bundle content for people in their organization, and one workspace can hold several org apps. Content from a single workspace can thereby reach people who have no workspace access. Supported included items are Power BI reports, paginated reports, Fabric notebooks, Fabric apps (preview), maps and real-time dashboards; dashboards and scorecards are not suitable. An org app has one overview page, navigation sections and links, a custom icon and theme color, and audiences that show different content to different groups; at least one audience always exists. Granting access to the app gives at least read access to the included items and to the underlying semantic model, even across workspaces, and removing app access withdraws what the app granted. Creating one needs a Pro, trial, Premium or Fabric workspace and an Admin, Member or Contributor role; Viewers cannot create them. Limitations include no report comments, no single sign-on for custom visuals, no audience tabs in the mobile apps, and no direct link to one audience.

power-bi-performance-analyzer.title: Use Performance Analyzer to examine report element performance – Microsoft Learn
power-bi-performance-analyzer.notes: Performance analyzer is a pane in Power BI Desktop report view and in the edit mode of a report in the Power BI service. It shows how long each visual needs to load, split into categories, so authors can find visuals or report elements that slow a report and see why. Interaction-driven loads, such as applying slicer filters, are measured as well. You start and stop a recording, and the results stay in the pane afterwards. Further controls clear the log, refresh all visuals on the page, analyze a single visual, export the results as a JSON file, and copy a visual's DAX query. For DirectQuery tables the copied query also includes the translated SQL or KQL. In Desktop the query can be run directly in DAX query view. The measured durations are grouped into DAX query, direct query, visual display, other and evaluated parameters (preview). Because most canvas and visual operations share one UI thread, reported times include time spent waiting in a queue. The queries generated by visuals are more verbose than necessary, and DAX speed depends on calculation complexity and on the number of tables and relationships. The page names no special licensing requirements.

power-bi-premium-per-user.title: Premium Per User (PPU) – Microsoft Fabric / Power BI – Microsoft Learn
power-bi-premium-per-user.notes: Premium Per User is a way to license Power BI Premium features on a per-person basis. It includes all Power BI Pro capabilities plus premium features such as the XMLA endpoint and AI features, so no separate Pro subscription is needed. It is described as the lowest entry point to Premium functionality, and it can be used alongside Premium capacities, although publishing into an existing capacity does not require it. Further features available per user include deployment pipelines, incremental refresh and advanced dataflow capabilities, while multi-geo support, unlimited distribution and on-premises report hosting are only offered with capacity licensing. Models are limited in size, and tenant storage has a ceiling. Anyone who opens content in a PPU workspace or app needs a PPU license, including for XMLA access, Analyze in Excel and composite models; with Power BI Embedded, every viewer needs one. Unlicensed users cannot use datasets and reports from PPU workspaces or Publish to web. Administrators manage licenses and workspaces in the admin portal and need not manage memory or CPU. Workspaces can move between PPU and a capacity, after which datasets must be refreshed fully. Data exchange across tenants is not possible with PPU.

power-bi-project-pbip.title: Power BI Desktop projects (PBIP) – Microsoft Learn
power-bi-project-pbip.notes: Saving as a Power BI project stores the report and semantic model definitions as individual plain-text files in a clear folder structure. The purpose is authoring, collaboration and versioning of Power BI content, especially with Git and CI/CD. A project consists of a semantic model folder, a report folder, a gitignore file created only if none exists, and a pbip file that points to the report folder and opens report and model together. Several reports and models can live in one directory. The text files can be edited in a code editor such as Visual Studio Code, and the model can also be changed through external tools or its TMDL files; Desktop notices external changes and asks to apply them, but the page warns that outside edits can cause unexpected behavior or, rarely, inconsistencies. Projects can be deployed with Fabric Git integration, the Fabric REST APIs or publishing from Desktop, which also transfers the local data cache. Limitations include no sensitivity labels, no direct saving to OneDrive or SharePoint, the Windows path length limit, no deployment to Analysis Services, and conversion between PBIX and PBIP only manually via Save as.

power-bi-relationships.title: Model relationships in Power BI Desktop – Microsoft Learn
power-bi-relationships.notes: A model relationship connects a column in one table to a column in another and passes filters between the tables, also across several tables, along deterministic paths. Relationships do not enforce data integrity. Both columns should share a data type. Cardinality can be one-to-many, many-to-one, one-to-one or many-to-many, and Desktop detects it automatically; the one side must hold unique values or the refresh fails. Filter direction is single or both, with one-to-one always both. Only one active path is allowed between a pair of tables, and inactive relationships are switched on in a measure with USERELATIONSHIP. Related DAX functions include RELATED, RELATEDTABLE, CROSSFILTER and TREATAS. Regular relationships expand tables with outer joins and show blank members for unmatched rows, whereas limited relationships, arising from many-to-many or cross source group links, do not. When several paths exist, priority and weight resolve ambiguity, and equal values cause an error. The recommended pattern is a star schema with a fact table and dimension tables. Role-playing dimensions use inactive relationships, and disconnected tables feed measures. Limits: no relationship between two columns of the same table, and bidirectional filters can hurt performance.

power-bi-report-themes.title: Use report themes in Power BI Desktop – Microsoft Learn
power-bi-report-themes.notes: Report themes, also called custom themes, apply design changes to a whole report: theme colors, default visual formatting and style presets. All visuals take the theme as their default style, and visuals using theme colors update automatically when the theme changes. A base theme maintained by Microsoft is added when a report is created and stays until it is updated; a custom theme sits above it and can override or extend it. Built-in themes include Bloom, Dark, Divergent, Frontier, Innovate, Soft dark, Tidal and Copilot default, and organizations can supply their own if the tenant admin provides them. A theme gallery offers community themes. In Desktop the Design ribbon offers customizing, importing and downloading themes; in the service the Theme pane under View is used. Broader changes require editing the JSON file, which can define names, data colors, background and foreground. Colors are assigned to series in the order of the theme colors. Applying a built-in or imported theme removes existing customizations, and visuals formatted individually are not overwritten until reset. Colors chosen via More colors do not follow a theme change. Reset to default also clears button actions and conditional formatting. The page names no licensing requirements.

power-bi-shape-map.title: Shape map visualization in Power BI – Microsoft Learn
power-bi-shape-map.notes: The shape map visual shows data on any shapes that can be defined, such as countries, regions, floor plans, seating charts or custom boundaries. Each area is colored according to the data so patterns and differences between regions become visible. It works in both Power BI Desktop and the Power BI service, and the page makes no statement about licensing. The field wells are Location, which holds a geographic field such as state, region or district, Color saturation, a numeric measure that drives the shading, and an optional Legend to classify regions. Under Format, the map settings let you choose a built-in map type, such as a country map, and a projection (equirectangular, Mercator or orthographic). Colors, blank-area color and border color and thickness can be adjusted. Custom maps are supplied as TopoJSON or GeoJSON files, uploaded or referenced by URL. TopoJSON extends GeoJSON by encoding topology, so shared borders are stored once and files tend to be smaller. A map that was uploaded can be downloaded for editing. Limitations: the color saturation field must be set for legend classification to work, there is an upper bound on data points, and three-letter ISO country codes are recommended because two-letter codes are sometimes not recognized.

power-bi-slicers.title: Slicers in Power BI – Microsoft Learn
power-bi-slicers.notes: Slicers are interactive filter controls placed directly on the report canvas. They narrow the part of the semantic model shown in other visuals without opening the filter pane, make frequently used filters visible, show the current filter state at a glance, and can filter by columns that are hidden in data tables. The page applies to Power BI Desktop and the Power BI service and names no license requirements. Several types exist: the standard slicer visual with vertical list, tiles, dropdown or date picker, where relative date selections are recalculated each time the report loads; the button slicer with styled buttons in grid layouts; the list slicer with images, labels, hierarchies, search and selection pills; and the input slicer for free text or number entry with operators. Slicers can be synchronized across pages or grouped by name, and visual interactions decide which visuals they filter or highlight; by default they also filter other slicers. An eraser icon clears a slicer's selections. Field parameters automatically create a slicer that lets users switch measures or dimensions. Values can be pasted from other applications, but only as exact matches and not into the input slicer. Selecting all values filters nothing, and deselecting uses a not-in filter.

power-bi-verified-answers.title: Verified answers – Prepare data for AI in Power BI – Microsoft Learn
power-bi-verified-answers.notes: Verified answers are human-approved visual responses in Power BI Copilot that are triggered by predefined phrases. Each one consists of at least one trigger phrase, a visual and optionally filters, and it is stored in the semantic model, so it applies to every report built on that model. Copilot first compares a prompt with the trigger phrases, either exactly or by semantic similarity, and if one matches it returns the verified answer instead of generating a new one. Users then see a verified checkmark, the trigger phrase, an AI text summary and a section explaining how Copilot arrived at the result. The goal is consistent, curated answers to common or complex questions. Authoring works in Power BI Desktop and in the service, requires Q&A to be turned on for the model, a Copilot-enabled workspace and write permission on the model. Limitations include no support for CI/CD, slicers, relative date filters, report themes, hidden fields or report measures, and several visual types such as custom visuals and decomposition trees. Row-level and object-level security are not fully supported, so the feature should not be relied on as a security control. Q&A is being retired, and the feature is not available when Fabric IQ is enabled.

power-bi-workspace-app.title: Apps in Power BI – Microsoft Learn
power-bi-workspace-app.notes: A workspace app is the long-standing form of Power BI app that bundles and publishes content from a workspace. It can exist next to org apps, a newer Fabric item type, and existing workspace apps are not renamed, migrated or replaced automatically. Designers use apps to give a broad audience, from individuals to a whole organization, curated content in one place, so business users do not have to hunt for individual dashboards and reports. An app can contain dashboards, reports, semantic models and spreadsheets, with navigation and design chosen by the designer. App permissions can differ from workspace permissions, which simplifies access management. To view an app, a recipient needs a Power BI Pro or Premium Per User license, or the app must be shared into Premium capacity. Users install apps from the Apps page via Get apps, through a direct link, or because the designer installed it automatically. The Get apps option is missing in the Power BI mobile app, where a link is needed. Users receive an email notification when they first get access or gain access to another audience. Published updates show the newest version without a notice, and data stays current as long as the semantic model refreshes on schedule.

power-pages-server-logic.title: Server logic overview – Power Pages – Microsoft Learn
power-pages-server-logic.notes: Server logic lets makers run JavaScript on the server to extend a Power Pages site at runtime. The code stays hidden from the browser and is protected by web roles and table permissions. Its purpose is to move critical operations out of the client for better control, scalability and security, to keep secrets, API keys and business rules away from the browser, and to maintain logic centrally across pages and forms. It is created in the design studio, written in Visual Studio Code with IntelliSense and compile-time validation, and stored in Dataverse, so lifecycle management and deployment pipelines apply as for other components. The language is native JavaScript following ECMAScript 2023 without browser APIs such as the DOM, fetch or XMLHttpRequest. Code can query, change and delete Dataverse data and call external REST APIs and Azure Functions. It is invoked through a site endpoint under the _api path, and each HTTP method maps to a function named get, post, put, patch or del. Every call needs a CSRF token, and the application session handles authentication. Tenant administrators can block outgoing HTTP calls per site, and site settings control the feature switch, allowed domains and timeout.

power-pages-table-permissions.title: Table permissions overview – Power Pages – Microsoft Learn
power-pages-table-permissions.notes: Table permissions control access to Dataverse records on Power Pages sites. Without them access is restricted by default, which covers forms, lists, Liquid, the Web API and other components that read Dataverse tables. A permission only takes effect when linked to at least one web role, and users in those roles receive the selected privileges. A permission has a name, a table, an access type, privileges, web roles and optionally child permissions related to a parent table. Access types are global, contact, account and self; a custom access type, shown as preview, uses a FetchXML filter and requires enhanced authorization, while the parent type exists only in the Portal Management app. Permissions can be created from a form or list component, from the Security workspace in the design studio, or in the Portal Management app. Contact and account access need a table relationship to the target table, which must be published and synced in the design studio. Child roles come from the parent permission. Disabling a parent makes its children ineffective, and deleting a parent deletes its children. For custom access only the filter element of the FetchXML is evaluated. Polymorphic lookups are not supported for parent-child permissions.

power-pages-web-api.title: Web API overview – Power Pages – Microsoft Learn
power-pages-web-api.notes: The Power Pages Web API is a REST-like interface that lets pages of a site create, read, update and delete Dataverse table rows. It follows a pattern similar to the Dataverse Web API but supports only a subset of it, and it is meant for richer user experiences, such as creating an account or updating a contact without a form. Requests go through the _api route of the site and use the entity set name, while site settings use the logical table name. Operations are case sensitive, and server-side caching makes later calls faster than the first. Each table must be enabled through site settings, which also list the permitted columns; a wildcard for all columns is deprecated, and columns can alternatively come from a dedicated system view. Access follows table permissions via web roles, column permissions can narrow it further, and every call needs a CSRF token, with the application session handling authentication. A Power Pages license is required, and anonymous calls count against anonymous-user capacity. Limitations: it is not optimized for third-party integration, does not support actions and functions, blocks configuration tables such as site settings and web pages, and has a known issue with multi-level table permissions that can be worked around with FetchXML.

power-platform-alm.title: Overview of application lifecycle management with Microsoft Power Platform – Microsoft Learn
power-platform-alm.notes: Application lifecycle management covers governance, development and maintenance of applications over their life, with disciplines such as requirements, architecture, development, testing, change management, deployment, release management and continuous integration. ALM tooling gives development teams and business units a standard way to communicate and can automate development and delivery, with predictable, repeatable software delivery as the aim. In Power Platform the central mechanism is solutions, which are exported and imported to move components between environments. Components include tables, columns, canvas and model-driven apps, Power Automate flows, agents, charts and plug-ins. Dataverse stores the artifacts, including solutions and in-product deployment pipelines. Source control is meant to be the source of truth, and a CI/CD platform such as Azure DevOps can automate build, test and deployment. The guidance applies to Power Apps, Power Automate, Power Pages, Copilot Studio and Dataverse. The one explicit prerequisite is that every participating environment contains a Dataverse database; source control and CI/CD are recommended rather than mandatory. No licensing requirements are listed.

power-platform-tenant-isolation.title: Cross-tenant inbound and outbound restrictions (tenant isolation) – Power Platform – Microsoft Learn
power-platform-tenant-isolation.notes: Tenant isolation lets administrators control inbound and outbound cross-tenant connections of Power Platform connectors based on the Microsoft Entra tenant. It applies only to connectors that authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID, such as Office 365 Outlook or SharePoint, and it is separate from the Entra-wide tenant restrictions feature, so access outside Power Platform is not affected. The aim is to keep connector use secure within the tenant and to reduce the risk of data exfiltration. By default the setting is off and cross-tenant connections work with valid Entra credentials. When switched on, all tenants are blocked in both directions except those on an allow list; entries apply to inbound, outbound or both, can be given as a domain or tenant ID, and a wildcard allows every tenant in a direction. It is configured in the Power Platform admin center under security and identity settings, and a Power Platform administrator role is mentioned for viewing and setting it. At design time, canvas apps cannot add the connection and flows are saved but suspended; at runtime violating apps and flows fail. Limitations: the Azure DevOps connector is not covered because of its own OAuth flow, and only canvas apps and flows are affected.

power-platform-tools-vs-code-extension.title: Install Power Platform Tools for Visual Studio Code – Microsoft Learn
power-platform-tools-vs-code-extension.notes: Power Platform Tools is an extension for Visual Studio Code, and the page presents it as the recommended way to install the Power Platform CLI, known as PAC CLI. The article explains how to install, update and uninstall the extension and how to manage authentication profiles. It can be installed from the Visual Studio Marketplace or from the Extensions view of VS Code by searching for its name, and it updates automatically when a new version appears, with a notification on startup. An earlier version can be chosen through the install-another-version option, which turns off automatic updates until the ignore-updates checkbox is cleared and VS Code restarted. Organizations that forbid web downloads can side-load it from a VSIX file. The prerequisites are an installed Visual Studio Code on Windows, Linux or macOS; the page states no license or cost information. Typical use is to run PAC CLI commands in the PowerShell terminal inside VS Code. By default the commands work only in that terminal. To use them from the Windows command prompt or regular PowerShell, one must install the CLI as a .NET tool, use the Windows MSI installer or add the CLI file to the PATH manually.

power-query-m.title: Power Query M formula language reference – Microsoft Learn
power-query-m.notes: Power Query M is the formula language used to express data mashups. A mashup filters and combines data from one or more of a large set of supported data sources, which is the core capability of Power Query. The language is functional, case sensitive and similar to F#. It is used in many places, among them Analysis Services in desktop form, Excel and Power BI workbooks, and online services such as Fabric, the Power BI service, Power Apps and Microsoft 365 Customer Insights. The documentation is organized into concepts, specification, reference and a getting-started area. The concepts cover expressions, values and the let expression, the evaluation model, types and type conversion, and how culture influences text formatting. The specification section contains the language specification and the type system. The reference lists functions, enumerations, constants and dynamic values. A quick tour of M and learning material about M functions help newcomers. This overview page itself does not state prerequisites, licensing or limits, and it contains no code samples, so such details have to be looked up in the linked subpages.

powerpages-chat-participant.title: Use GitHub Copilot Chat with Power Pages (@powerpages) – Microsoft Learn
powerpages-chat-participant.notes: The @powerpages chat participant is part of the Power Platform Tools extension for Visual Studio Code and plugs into GitHub Copilot Chat through the Copilot Chat extension API. It brings Power Pages coding help directly into the chat, so developers need not leave their VS Code workspace. Two capabilities are described: writing code, for example JavaScript for form field validation, and explaining code, for example a Liquid include. Answers are tailored to Power Pages. The prerequisites are VS Code, the Power Platform Tools extension and a configured GitHub Copilot Chat extension. To work with site content, the site is downloaded into VS Code with the Power Platform CLI, which requires authentication against a Microsoft Dataverse environment. The typical flow is to download the site content, open Copilot Chat, confirm it is active and type @powerpages followed by the request. The feature is marked as preview, is not intended for production use, may have limited functionality and its documentation may change. The page gives no licensing or cost details.

project-schedule-api.title: Use Project Schedule APIs to perform operations with scheduling entities – Microsoft Learn
project-schedule-api.notes: The Project Schedule APIs allow creating, updating and deleting scheduling entities that are managed by the scheduling engine of Project for the web; earlier releases restricted these operations. They apply to Project Operations integrated with ERP and to Project Operations Core. An OperationSet acts as a unit of work so several schedule-related requests are handled within one transaction. Scheduling entities include project, project task, task dependency, resource assignment, bucket, team member, checklist, label, sprint and the link between task and label. The API set contains actions to create a project and a team member, which create records immediately and so cannot be used inside an OperationSet, plus actions to create an OperationSet, create, update and delete records, and execute the OperationSet. Another action updates the planned work contour of a resource assignment. Support differs per entity; for instance task dependencies can only be created or deleted, and projects cannot be deleted. Only users holding a Microsoft Project license can call these APIs, so application users, system users and integration users cannot. Limits apply to operations per set and open sets per user, and status and error logs for operation sets were noted as unavailable.

protected-users.title: Protected Users Security Group – Microsoft Learn
protected-users.notes: Protected Users is a global security group in Active Directory designed to guard against credential theft. When a member signs in, non-configurable protections on the device prevent credentials from being cached: CredSSP and WDigest do not store plaintext credentials, NTLM stores neither plaintext credentials nor the one-way function, Kerberos creates no DES or RC4 keys, and no cached verifier is made, so offline sign-in is impossible. On domain controllers, members cannot authenticate with NTLM, DES or RC4 in Kerberos pre-authentication, and neither unconstrained nor constrained delegation is allowed; the ticket-granting ticket lifetime is fixed. Requirements include recent Windows clients, a domain functional level of Windows Server 2012 R2 or higher, and AES keys on the account. Members are added through the Active Directory administrative tools or with the Add-ADGroupMember cmdlet. The group has the well-known RID 525, no default members, and is not protected by AdminSDHolder. Service and computer accounts must not be added, because the local protections do not work for them. Privileged accounts should be added only after testing to avoid lockouts. Optional authentication logs, off by default, record client and domain controller events. The page lists no license requirements.

provision-on-demand.title: On-demand provisioning in Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync – Microsoft Learn
provision-on-demand.notes: On-demand provisioning in Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync lets an administrator test configuration changes on a single user. The goal is to check that changes are applied correctly and synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID. The article covers only the direction from Active Directory to Entra ID; the opposite direction has its own article. The administrator signs in to the Entra admin center with at least the Hybrid Identity Administrator role, opens an existing Cloud Sync configuration, chooses provision on demand and enters the distinguished name of the user. After a successful run the interface shows four green checkmarks, and errors appear to the left of them. The details are split into four stages: importing the user from Active Directory including attributes from custom mappings, determining whether the user is in scope, matching the user between source and target to decide on create, update or delete, and performing the action, which shows the resulting state in Entra ID and helps trace attribute transformations. Typical use is validating configuration changes before they are rolled out broadly. A notable caveat is that scoping filters are not applied to the selected user, so users outside the configured organizational units can be provisioned.

psreadline.title: PSReadLine Module – PowerShell – Microsoft Learn
psreadline.notes: PSReadLine is a PowerShell module with cmdlets for customizing command-line editing. Its documented cmdlets are Get-PSReadLineKeyHandler and Get-PSReadLineOption for reading key bindings and configurable options, Set-PSReadLineKeyHandler for binding keys to custom or built-in handler functions, Remove-PSReadLineKeyHandler for removing a binding, and Set-PSReadLineOption for changing how editing behaves. The function PSConsoleHostReadLine is the main entry point of the module. The page lists which PSReadLine version ships with which PowerShell release, starting with the version bundled in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and continuing through successive PowerShell 7 releases. The target platforms are Windows, macOS and Linux, and the page names no other prerequisites and no license or cost information. Typical use is tuning the console, such as defining shortcuts or adjusting editor options. One limitation concerns accessibility: since PowerShell 7.0, PowerShell does not load PSReadLine automatically on Windows when a screen reader is detected, because the module currently does not work well with screen readers. The default rendering in that case works correctly, and the module can still be loaded manually.

q-sharp.title: Overview of the Q# quantum programming language – Microsoft Learn
q-sharp.notes: Q# is a high-level, open-source programming language from Microsoft for writing quantum programs, and it belongs to the Microsoft Quantum Development Kit. Qubits are not tied to particular hardware; compiler and runtime map program qubits onto physical ones, so the same code can target different processors. The language supports combining quantum and classical computation and offers built-in operations for superposition, entanglement and measurement. Physical rules apply: qubit states cannot be copied or read out directly. A program may use one namespace, and its entry point is a Main operation or any operation marked with the EntryPoint attribute. Types include Int, Double, Bool, String, ranges, arrays and tuples plus Qubit and Result, whose value is Zero or One. Qubits are allocated with use and start in the zero state; they must be returned to zero before release or a runtime error occurs. Measurement works in Pauli bases. Core and intrinsic standard library namespaces load automatically, others must be imported. Q# code can be simulated locally or run in Jupyter notebooks, and the resource estimator needs no Azure account, while running on real quantum hardware requires an Azure account and a quantum workspace.

query-diagnostics.title: Query diagnostics – Power Query – Microsoft Learn
query-diagnostics.notes: Query diagnostics shows what Power Query does while authoring and refreshing in Power BI Desktop. It helps identify which queries are sent to the data source, where slowdowns occur and which background events take place. The feature is on the Tools tab of the Power Query editor ribbon. By default it may need administrator rights, depending on IT policy; without them an option in the Desktop diagnostics settings allows tracing only inside the editor, covering preview and authoring but not a full refresh. You start and stop diagnostics, and traces are lost if you never stop. A separate action runs diagnostics for just the selected step. Output comes in primary diagnostics, available as a summarized or a detailed view, data privacy partitions that show the logical partitions used for privacy, and performance counters that sample resource use regularly. Important columns include the Id, the data source query, which also reveals whether folding was complete, and a flag separating user-created from system-generated queries. Exclusive duration percentages add up to about a hundred percent only within one Id. Caching can distort comparisons between steps, some columns exist only for certain connectors, and Power Query also issues queries the user did not trigger directly.
